translations.text: His father did not restrain him and never said, “Why have you done this?” He was handsome in appearance, and he was born after Absalom.
All Adonijah’s guests were frightened, rose, and went away, each on his own way.
King Solomon sent for him and had him brought down from the altar. He came and bowed to the ground before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, “Go to your house.”
He said, “I have something to say to you.” She said, “Speak.”
King Solomon swore by the Lord and said, “May God do so to me, and more besides, if Adonijah has not spoken these words against his own life.”
Benaiah son of Jehoiada went out, struck Joab, and killed him. He buried him at his own house in the wilderness.
“And now, why have you not kept the oath sworn by the Lord and the command that I gave you?”
“And now, Lord my God, you have placed your servant in place of David my father. But I am a little child and do not know how to go out or come in.”
This woman’s son died during the night because she lay on him.
“She rose in the middle of the night and took my child from my arms while your servant was asleep. She laid him in her own bosom and laid her dead son in my bosom.”

The other woman said, “No, your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.” But the first woman said, “No, my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.” So they spoke before the king.
For he ruled over everything beyond the river, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kingdoms on that side of the river. He had peace on every side around him.
Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, because he heard that they had anointed him king in place of David his father, for Hiram had always loved David.
Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying:
In the four hundred and fortieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, in the fourth year of King Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the second month, he began building the house of the Lord.

The lowest side chamber was five cubits wide, the middle one six cubits wide, and the third seven cubits wide. For he made offsets around the outside of the house, so that the beams would not be driven into the walls of the house.
The entrance to the side chamber was below, on the right side of the house. A winding stairway led up to the middle story, and from the middle to the third story.
Solomon built the house and completed it.
The house, the inner temple, was forty cubits long.
The space before the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid it with refined gold and made an altar of fir wood.
For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made doors of juniper wood and fivefold doorframes.
On their panels, between the supports, were lions, bulls, and cherubim, and likewise on the supports above. Below the lions and bulls were spaces with [?] work.
There were four supports at the four corners of each stand; its supports were part of the stand itself.
On the bank of the Jordan, in the thick soil between Succoth and Zarethan, he cast these things for the king.
The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house.
So that they may fear you all their days, as long as they live on the face of the earth that you gave to our fathers.

For they will sin against you, since there is no one who does not sin; and if you turn against them and hand them over to their enemies, and their captors carry them away to an enemy’s land, far away or nearby,
And the king and all the Israelites with him offered sacrifices before the Lord.
Hiram king of Tyre supplied Solomon with fir wood, cedar wood, gold, and everything he wanted. Then King Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in Galilee.
And Baalath and Thermoth in the wilderness, in that land.
But Pharaoh’s daughter went up from the City of David to her own house, which he had built for her. Then he built the Millo.
And the queen of Sheba heard of Solomon’s fame, the name of the Lord, and Solomon’s wisdom, and she came to test him with riddles.
And Solomon did evil before the Lord and did not follow the Lord as his father David had.
For Joab and all Israel stayed there in Edom for six months, until he had destroyed every male among the Edomites.
And Hadad himself and all the Edomite men who were servants of his father fled and went into Egypt. Hadad was a small child.
And the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
And all Israel came to King Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had told them, saying, “Return to me on the third day.”

And the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was from the Lord, so that the Lord might establish his word, which he had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.

And King Jeroboam said to the man of God, “Please seek the favor of the Lord your God and pray for me, so that my hand may be restored to me.” And the man of God pleaded before the Lord, and the king’s hand was restored to him and became as it had been before.
And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under the oak. He said to him, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” And he said, “I am.”
And take in your hand bread for the man of God, cakes for his sons, raisins, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the child.
Go and say to Jeroboam, “Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Because I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel,
And the rest of Rehoboam’s deeds and everything he did—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijah son of Rehoboam became king over Judah.
And he followed the sins his father had committed before the Lord his God, and his heart was not fully devoted to the Lord his God, as the heart of his father David had been.
And in the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned for twenty-four years.
And the rest of Elah’s deeds and everything he did—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And when Zimri saw that the city had been taken, he entered a chamber in the king’s house and burned the king’s house down over himself.
And Ahab made a grove, and Ahab did more to provoke the Lord, the God of Israel, than all the kings of Israel who had been before him.
And Elijah went and did according to the word of the Lord. He went and stayed in the ravine of Cherith, opposite the Jordan.
And he breathed on the child three times and called on the Lord, saying, “O Lord my God, let this child’s breath return to him.”
And Obadiah said, “What sin have I committed that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to kill me?”
“Was my lord not told what I did when Jezebel was slaughtering the Lord’s prophets? I hid a hundred men from among the Lord’s prophets, fifty men in each cave, and fed them with bread and water.”
And Elijah said, “As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will appear before him today.”
And Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of approaching rain.”

And he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness. He went and sat beneath a terebinth tree and asked that he might die, saying, “It is enough now, Lord. Take my life from me, Lord, for I am no better than my fathers.”
And Elijah looked, and there at his head were a cake of spelt and a jug of water. He got up, ate and drank, and lay down to sleep again.
And the elders and all the people said to him, “Do not listen and do not agree.”
And a man from among the sons of the prophets said to his companion, by the word of the Lord, “Strike me.” But the man would not strike him.
And his wife Jezebel said to him, “Is this how you exercise kingship over Israel? Get up, eat some bread, and regain your composure. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.”
And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Is there perhaps a prophet of the Lord here or not, so that we may inquire of the Lord through him?”
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself iron horns and said, “This is what the Lord says: With these you will gore the Syrians until they are wiped out.”

And Micaiah said, “Not so—not I. But hear the message of the Lord. Did I not indeed see the Lord, the God of Israel, seated on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing around him, on his right and on his left?”
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “I will disguise myself and go into battle, and you put on my clothes.” And the king of Israel disguised himself and entered the battle.
And Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah; he became king in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
And he served the Baals and bowed down to them, and provoked the Lord, the God of Israel, to anger, just as all those before him had done.
